title: Classification of Viral Genomes and Estimation of tMRCA of SARS-CoV-2 Using Phylodynamic Analysis
author: Xiaowen Hu
license_note: PMC full-text XML — Bio-protocol — CC-BY confirmed in article XML
materials:
Materials and reagents SARS-CoV-2 genome sequences were obtained from the GISAID database [13] on May 1,
2022. Genomes that were collected from hosts other than humans and/or had a length
of less than 2,900 nucleotides and more than 0.05% of unknown nucleotides were
filtered out. More than 5 million genomes were retained for further analysis.
The sample collection date is located in column

steps.title: Set up Conda environment and tools
steps.instruction: Create a fresh Conda environment and install all required bioinformatics software.

substeps.instruction: Add Conda to PATH: $ export PATH="/$HOME/miniconda/bin:$PATH"
Create Python 3.9 environment: $ conda create -n myenv python=3.9
Activate the environment: $ conda activate myenv
Install Seqkit: $ conda install -c bioconda seqkit
Install minimap2: $ git clone https://github.com/lh3/minimap2 && cd minimap2 && make && cd ..
Install ViralMSA: $ wget "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/niemasd/ViralMSA/master/ViralMSA.py" && chmod a+x ViralMSA.py && sudo mv ViralMSA.py /usr/local/bin/ViralMSA.py
Install CD‑HIT: $ git clone https://github.com/weizhongli/cdhit.git && cd cdhit && make && cd cd-hit-auxtools && make && cd ../..
Install ALTER: $ git clone https://github.com/sing-group/ALTER.git && cd ALTER && $HOME/apache-maven-3.8.4/bin/mvn && cd ..

steps.title: Download and unpack genomes
steps.instruction: Obtain SARS‑CoV‑2 FASTA and metadata files from GISAID and extract them.

substeps.instruction: Log in to GISAID and download the files (e.g., sequences_fasta_2022_04_29.tar.xz and metadata_tsv_2022_04_29.tar.xz).
Decompress and extract: $ xz -d sequences_fasta_2022_04_29.tar.xz && tar -xvf sequences_fasta_2022_04_29.tar
Decompress and extract metadata: $ xz -d metadata_tsv_2022_04_29.tar.xz && tar -xvf metadata_tsv_2022_04_29.tar

steps.title: Rename FASTA taxa to accessions
steps.instruction: Replace FASTA headers with GISAID accession numbers using the provided Perl script.

steps.title: Fetch GISAID reference sequence
steps.instruction: Create a file with the reference accession and extract the reference FASTA.

substeps.instruction: $ cat sequence.fasta | $HOME/seqkit grep -f accession.txt -t dna -j 10 -o reference_wiv04.fasta

steps.title: Filter metadata for human complete genomes
steps.instruction: Select entries that are from human hosts, have complete genomes and high coverage.

steps.title: Filter for accurate collection dates
steps.instruction: Remove records with missing or ambiguous sample dates using the custom Perl script.

steps.title: Extract accession list of filtered genomes
steps.instruction: Print the accession column (column 3) of the date‑filtered metadata to a text file.

steps.title: Retrieve filtered genome sequences
steps.instruction: Pull the FASTA records that match the filtered accession list.

steps.title: Align genomes with ViralMSA
steps.instruction: Run ViralMSA on the filtered FASTA using the reference and omit the reference from the output.

steps.title: Extract six linked nucleotide sites
steps.instruction: Use the provided Perl script to pull nucleotides at positions 241, 3037, 8782, 14408, 23403, and 28144 from the alignment.

steps.title: Classify genomes into three haplotypes
steps.instruction: Separate genomes based on the six‑site pattern using seqkit grep.

steps.title: Summarize haplotype statistics
steps.instruction: Generate basic statistics for each haplotype file and concatenate them into a single report.

steps.title: Export accession lists for each haplotype
steps.instruction: Create plain‑text files containing the accession numbers of genomes in each haplotype.

steps.title: Retrieve aligned sequences per haplotype
steps.instruction: Extract the aligned FASTA records for each haplotype using the accession lists.

steps.title: Identify early‑pandemic genomes
steps.instruction: Select genomes collected from December 2019 through April 2020.

steps.title: Retrieve aligned early‑genome sequences
steps.instruction: Extract the aligned FASTA records for the early‑pandemic accession list.

steps.title: Extract six sites from early genomes
steps.instruction: Run the same Perl script on the early‑genome alignment.

steps.title: Classify early genomes into haplotypes
steps.instruction: Separate early genomes using the six‑site patterns.

steps.title: Export accession lists for early haplotypes
steps.instruction: Create accession files for each early haplotype.

steps.title: Retrieve aligned sequences for early haplotypes
steps.instruction: Extract aligned FASTA records for each early haplotype using the accession lists.

substeps.instruction: $ cat global_early_all_haplotype.fasta.aln | $HOME/seqkit grep -f global_early_DS.accessions.txt -t dna -j 10 -o global_early_DS.aln
$ cat global_early_all_haplotype.fasta.aln | $HOME/seqkit grep -f global_early_DL.accessions.txt -t dna -j 10 -o global_early_DL.aln
$ cat global_early_all_haplotype.fasta.aln | $HOME/seqkit grep -f global_early_GL.accessions.txt -t dna -j 10 -o global_early_GL.aln

steps.title: Filter haplotype alignments for unknown bases
steps.instruction: Remove sequences with >0.05 % ambiguous nucleotides from each haplotype alignment.

steps.title: Convert collection dates to decimal format
steps.instruction: Transform the original date strings into decimal years for BEAST input.

steps.title: Build BEAST XML file with BEAUti
steps.instruction: Create the BEAST configuration on a Windows machine using BEAUti v1.10.4.

substeps.instruction: Open BEAUti‑v1.10.4 by double‑clicking its icon.
Load the early‑genome alignment (converted to NEX format).
Set clock model to either ‘strict’ or ‘relaxed’.
Set tree prior to ‘Bayesian Skyline’ or ‘Bayesian SkyGrid’.
Set MCMC chain length to 1,200,000,000 generations.
Ensure the Expected Sample Size (ESS) for all parameters will exceed 200 before final run.
Click ‘Generate BEAST file’ and save the XML.

steps.title: Run BEAST phylogenetic analysis
steps.instruction: Execute the BEAST XML on Windows; the run may take several days until ESS >200.

substeps.instruction: Open BEAST v1.10.4 by double‑clicking its icon.
Load the generated BEAST XML file.
Press ‘Run’. Monitor the log; continue until all ESS values are >200.

steps.title: Visualize tMRCA with Tracer
steps.instruction: Inspect the posterior distribution of the time to most recent common ancestor using Tracer v1.7.2.

substeps.instruction: Open Tracer v1.7.2 by double‑clicking its icon.
Import the BEAST log file produced in the previous step.
Select ‘age(root)’ and view the ‘Marginal Density’ plot.
Read the mean tMRCA and 95 % HPD interval from the ‘Estimates’ tab.
